items.title: Data-efficient molecular and nanoparticle design via fine-tuned large language models
items.abstract_or_text: Designing molecules with prescribed properties is central to pharmaceutical and materials innovation, but vast chemical design spaces make development lengthy and costly. Generative artificial intelligence can accelerate molecular discovery, but its deployment in many real-world domains remains limited by the need for large task-specific training datasets. To enable generative design when property-labeled data are scarce, we present a data-efficient foundation-model adaptation strategy combining complementary positive and negative property prompts with parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Generated molecules are then ranked by molecular graph-kernel Gaussian process regression for structure-aware prioritization. In a controlled computational setting, the platform generated candidates with novel scaffolds satisfying multiple design objectives, including predicted target binding, synthesizability, and drug-likeness. Although only a few hundred training molecules per target met all three criteria, the model generated thousands of new molecules matching the desired profiles. For prospective validation, we applied the model to nanoparticle design, a domain of high clinical potential but limited excipient diversity. Fine-tuning on only 1,521 labeled drug-excipient pairs - including just 139 nanoparticle-forming examples identified new nanoparticle-forming excipients for the anticancer drug sorafenib. The model proposed lithocholic acid and the sorafenib metabolite M6, and experiments confirmed that both form stable sorafenib nanoparticles with high encapsulation efficiency and increased in vitro potency. These findings show that foundation-model fine-tuning with complementary prompts and graph-based prioritization enables data-efficient molecular design in low-data chemical domains.

items.title: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
items.abstract_or_text: Chemistry has recently entered a high-data regime as molecular databases from high-throughput platforms or computational studies have become available. Increasing automation within the chemical sciences leads to a more digital and precision chemistry. Dedicated scientific agents are becoming central to guiding the chemist through an ever-increasing amount of data and findings, including negative ones. Here, we introduce Magnolia, a persistent-memory artificial intelligence agent framework that integrates computational protocols, from docking to quantum chemistry, lab notebooks and chat logs relying on large language models (LLMs). It relies on a three-tier memory system: session-level observations are automatically captured and distilled into structured learnings, confirmed and elevated to project-tier entries and, when human-validated, promoted to cross-project rules that actively guide subsequent work and provide direct chemical feedback. We illustrate Magnolia on four case studies: quantum-chemical evaluation of aromatic systems (COMPAS database), molecular dynamics of butane and of modified DNA, and a protein-peptide docking campaign. Across these projects, Magnolia tracked 317 runs and accumulated 116 project-tier entries, from which four cross-project rules were promoted; in controlled replays of four tasks, runs with memory passed the checks that runs without it failed (for example, ten of ten docking-configuration checks, against one to four of ten). By combining automation, reproducibility, and human-in-the-loop control, our Magnolia framework streamlines docking, molecular dynamics and quantum chemistry calculations with direct analysis and LLM-augmented feedback, offering accelerated access to computational (bio)chemistry.

items.title: HierDTA: Hierarchical Structure-Aware Representation Learning for Drug--Target Affinity Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Drug--target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computer-aided drug discovery, where reliable computational models can help prioritize compound--protein pairs before experimental validation. A key challenge in DTA prediction is to effectively mine multi-level molecular information from drug structures while accurately modeling the binding-site environment of target proteins. To address these issues, we introduce HierDTA, a hierarchical structure-aware framework for DTA prediction. black{HierDTA represents each drug as an atom--motif heterogeneous graph and introduces an augmentation module that propagates functional-motif semantics to the corresponding atoms. For proteins, kinase-domain structures are converted into residue interaction graphs. The resulting atom and residue representations are integrated using cross-attention to capture pair-specific relationships, while molecule fingerprints and pretrained ESM-2 embeddings provide complementary global information. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, HierDTA achieves superior performance on the Davis dataset across all metrics and attains the highest \(r_m^2\) of 0.791 on KIBA. It also exhibits strong generalization under cold-start settings, particularly on KIBA, where MSE is reduced by 21.7\% in the unseen-protein scenario. Ablation study and interpretability analysis supported the contributions of the hierarchical augmentation and interaction components.} Case studies further showed that HierDTA provided early enrichment of candidate bioactive compounds. These results indicate that HierDTA is an effective framework for affinity prediction and target-specific virtual screening.

items.title: Reliable and Efficient Agentic Protein Design with Toolset Harnessing
items.abstract_or_text: Computational protein design workflows require the orchestration of multiple tools, data formats, and analysis steps that are often fragmented. Here, we introduce Chaperone, a lightweight and customizable framework that enables seamless integration of RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) with downstream sequence design, structure prediction, and evaluation tools, including ProteinMPNN, AlphaFold3 (AF3), and more than 50 other protein design tools. By combining a programmable agent-friendly interface with parallelized execution on high-performance computing systems, Chaperone as a harness enables rapid iteration and scalable exploration of complex protein design workflows. Across an evaluation of nine biomolecular design tasks, we find using Chaperone reduces total token usage relative to baseline agents by 86% and GPU costs by 64%, while increasing the overall computational design pass rate. We demonstrate Chaperones utility for large-scale design-space exploration through a two-week end-to-end small-molecule binder design campaign, yielding low nanomolar binders to cortisol zero shot. We further demonstrate its versatility across distinct design challenges, including the design of a symmetric 12-subunit self-assembly nanoparticle and a linker that mediates interactions between C2- and D3-symmetric protein complexes to form crystalline assemblies. Together, these results demonstrate how agent harnesses built around standardized tool interfaces can substantially improve the efficiency and success of complex, long-horizon agentic design workflows in biology. We make Chaperone freely available to the community on GitHub: https://github.com/RosettaCommons/chaperone.

items.title: Genetically programmable molecular framework for constructing precision recombinant human ECM mimics
items.abstract_or_text: Engineering extracellular matrix (ECM) mimetic materials that combine molecular precision of synthetic material options with native biological complexity remains a central challenge in biomaterials science. Here, we present a genetically programmable hydrogel platform that enables independent control of mechanical and biological properties including matrix composition, mechanics, viscoelasticity, and biochemical signaling using recombinant human ECM building blocks assembled via isopeptide chemistry. Modular protein ECM crosslinkers containing complete folded ECM domains equipped with terminal SpyTag peptides were integrated within SpyCatcher-functionalized interchangeable natural polysaccharide backbones to generate fully defined matrices with decoupled material parameters. Point mutations on crosslinker SpyTags within the bond interface varied bond affinity from covalent to physical bonding, allowing tuned stress-relaxation behaviors across physiologically relevant regimes without altering matrix composition nor stiffness. Using colorectal cancer models, we show that polymer identity and matrix viscoelasticity independently regulate spheroid growth, invasion capabilities, and dispersion. Importantly, recombinant ECM domains recapitulated native adhesion functions and provide a structurally encoded layer of biological information. This hydrogel platform provides a molecular framework for constructing precision recombinant human ECM mimics with broad applicability across biomaterials science, mechanobiology, disease modeling, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine.

items.title: Conditional latent distillation enables controllable molecular generation in data-limited soft materials
items.abstract_or_text: De novo molecular generation is particularly difficult when materials-specific datasets are too small to support reliable training of a new generative backbone. We develop a framework for controllable molecular generation based on conditional latent distillation and chemistryconstrained construction. A variational autoencoder (VAE) pretrained on more than 20,000 polymer molecules supplies a starting molecular representation, reducing reliance on training a new generator from approximately 1,600 surfactant or 200 anion-exchange-membrane (AEM) records. A compact conditional student learns to predict teacher latent coordinates from molecular descriptors and property-associated inputs, while molecular exploration and chemistry-aware editing govern which candidate structures are constructed and retained. In the primary surfactant application, Bayesian optimization produced 841 cleaned novel structures and retained 118, compared with 205 and 15 from nearest-neighbor exploration under equal 20,000-attempt mutation budgets. An independent distillation-guided teacher-latent retrieval benchmark yielded 2.32 more retained candidates per request than anchor-count-matched random selection (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.78–2.86). The conditional mapping also reduced teacher-coordinate prediction error by 40.3% and decoderdistribution divergence by 59.1% relative to the strongest tested regression baselines, validating the distillation-based interface. Molecular dynamics characterized selected surfactants at a water–decane interface. We then applied the chemistry-constrained construction and screening workflow to AEM-related building blocks, obtaining 125 screened candidates and assessing selected cations in water. These results demonstrate controllable molecular exploration and structural selection in data-limited settings, without claiming experimentally verified control of final materials properties.

items.title: Scaling Synthetic Pre-training Data and Evaluation for Indic LLMs
items.abstract_or_text: Building capable language models for India requires scalable multilingual data and robust evaluation. We introduce Nemotron-Pretraining-Indic-v1, a synthetic pretraining corpus of approximately 2.83 trillion tokens covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages in native script and twelve in romanized form. It is the largest openly released Indic pretraining corpus. Using our GPU-accelerated pipeline, we translate curated English documents, assess translation quality, and repair low-quality outputs while preserving technical content and document structure and maintaining source traceability. Through continued-pretraining experiments across twelve languages, we show that combining our synthetic corpus with natural Indic text improves knowledge and reasoning over a public-corpus baseline. Additional experiments show how data volume, script coverage, and Indic training share affect English performance. We also introduce the Indic-LLM-Eval-Suite, a multilingual benchmark suite for evaluating Indic language models across chat, instruction following, reasoning, knowledge, code, and translation. The suite combines existing Indic benchmarks with task-aware translations of English benchmarks, using automated quality assessment, targeted correction, and native-speaker review in a human-in-the-loop pipeline. We use the suite to comprehensively benchmark contemporary open-weight Indic and multilingual models across capabilities and languages, revealing substantial variation across tasks and languages. Together, these resources provide a scalable foundation for developing and evaluating more capable Indic language models.

items.title: Learning Protein-Protein Interaction Interfaces from Multimodal Representations
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Protein-protein interactions govern essential cellular processes, making the identification of interface residues critical for protein engineering and molecular design. Although complex deep learning algorithms like AlphaFold3 generate full atom resolution assemblies, they are not optimized for residue-level interface identification. Existing methods face inherent limitations: sequence-based models lack explicit 3D context, while structure-based approaches can overlook evolutionary signals. Results: By combining evolutionary context with 3D geometry, the multimodal protein language model ESM3 offers the ideal foundation for residue-level interface classification. This results in the ESM3-PPISites model, which outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods across diverse training and benchmark sets. Generalization is assessed through stringent sequence- and structure-based redundancy filtering to ensure evaluation on previously unseen proteins. Notably, finetuning the open-weight ESM3 architecture meaningfully narrows the performance gap with its proprietary full-scale counterpart. Furthermore, integrating predicted interaction sites as spatial restraints into HADDOCK significantly improves the recovery of near-native binding poses while reducing computational search time by an order of magnitude compared with blind docking. Conclusions: ESM3-PPISites enables accurate interfaces identification without relying on complex structural inputs at inference time, establishing a reliable and computationally efficient strategy for mapping protein-protein interaction sites.

items.title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
items.abstract_or_text: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.

items.title: Learning Inter-Graph Interactions Between Heterogeneous Substructures of Chemical Systems
items.abstract_or_text: Complex chemical systems containing heterogeneous substructures are common in real-world applications. Various physical phenomena of the complex chemical systems are derived from the interactions between the heterogeneous substructures. However, existing graph representation learning methods for inter-graph interactions assumed graph-level interactions between homogeneous structures, such as organic molecules and inorganic crystalline materials. We propose a data descriptor of the complex chemical systems and a graph neural network for learning inter-graph interactions between organic and inorganic compounds. We applied the proposed method to predict the physical properties of hybrid solar cell materials containing heterogeneous substructures, which have received significant attention for sustainable energy resources. By learning heterogeneous inter-graph interactions, the proposed method achieved state-of-the-art accuracy in predicting band gaps of 1,682 hybrid solar cell materials.

items.title: Accelerating Catalyst Discovery with Artificial Intelligence Using Molecular Dual-Atom Site Catalysts as a Case Study
creators: Bruno Ina cio da Silva Roux Leite
items.abstract_or_text: We test whether researchers can delegate the writing of a complete catalyst study to a large language model while retaining scientific judgment. Our case study concerns molecular dual-atom site catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction, where stabilizing an adsorbed intermediate can make its subsequent reduction less favorable. Using density functional theory calculations on 88 catalysts, we explain this balance through adsorption free energies and the overpotential volcano. We then use adsorbate specific ridge models to predict adsorption energies for 1,260 additional structures and identify candidates for further study. Among candidates with low predicted overpotentials, we find predominantly Fe adsorption centers, with separate structural patterns associated with S bridges and 1,2phenylenediamine. To communicate the reasoning behind these choices, we guided a large language model with explicit scientific writing instructions and refined its explanations through repeated scientific and editorial review. The resulting article is the demonstration: we delegate manuscript preparation while retaining responsibility for its scientific meaning. This approach to accelerating catalyst discovery with artificial intelligence offers researchers an opportunity to concentrate on scientific investigation while guiding how their results are communicated.

items.title: Machine Learning for Ionic Conductivity Prediction in Polymer Electrolytes: A Benchmark on Lithium Systems and a Feasibility Study on the Data-Scarce Multivalent (Mg, Zn, Na) Frontier
items.abstract_or_text: Solid and gel polymer electrolytes are central to safer, more flexible batteries, and machine learning has been used to predict their ionic conductivity directly from composition and processing variables. Almost all of this work targets lithium-ion systems, for which large, curated datasets exist. Polymer electrolytes conducting multivalent or non-lithium cations (magnesium, zinc, sodium) are promising lower-cost alternatives but remain comparably underexplored, in part because no public, ML-ready dataset of their measured ionic conductivities exists. Here we validate a standard composition-to-conductivity pipeline (Random Forest and XGBoost regression) on OBELiX, a published dataset of 599 lithium solid-state electrolytes, reaching R2 = 0.79 against a mean-predicting baseline near zero. We then construct, to our knowledge, the first ML-ready dataset of Mg-, Zn-, and Na-conducting polymer electrolytes, systematically mined from the primary and review literature: 135 data points across 105 distinct host-polymer/salt systems. Applying the same pipeline to this new dataset, a tuned Random Forest reaches R2 = 0.47 under leave-one-out cross-validation, or 0.36 under a more conservative 5-fold estimate, well below the lithium benchmark. Through chemistry-informed feature engineering and a nested cross-validation check, we show this gap is driven primarily by data scarcity and literature measurement heterogeneity, not by model or feature choice. We argue the scarcity is itself the central finding: it puts a number, for the first time, on how far behind the multivalent and non-lithium polymer electrolyte literature sits relative to the lithium-ion mainstream. We release the curated dataset and pipeline to support future community data collection.

items.title: LeakBench: Auditing Reward Hacking through Prediction-Time Leakage in Clinical Modeling Agents
items.abstract_or_text: Autonomous clinical-modeling agents can optimize predictive performance while violating conditions that make a model usable. We introduce LeakBench, an executable, guideline-derived audit suite that tests agent decisions for prediction-time leakage, calibration, site-level evaluation, support awareness, and decision-curve net benefit. LeakBench combines a synthetic task with known failure structure and two real-data settings: MIMIC-IV (430k admissions) and governed multi-hospital inpatient record front-page (MHFP) data. Our primary analysis uses reward hacking descriptively, without attributing intent: an agent selects prediction-time-invalid inputs because they improve its validation reward. A deterministic optimizer and every evaluated unconstrained local-model configuration select a fatal leaking feature. In fully logged September 2026 A/B runs, DeepSeek Flash and GPT-6-astra each leak in 10/10 unconstrained runs and 0/10 runs with an explicit admission-time constraint. This contrast is version-sensitive: a blinded Claude/Fable-5.1 chat run does not leak in either condition, while explicit-constraint violations appear only in a historical August 2026 slice lacking raw trajectories. Replacing AUROC with AUPRC does not remove leakage selection. Renaming or disguising the leaking inputs changes neither selection nor provenance-based detection; a name-based filter fails. A deterministic provenance verifier-in-loop removes the leak, making the LLM repair loop defense-in-depth. Specific verifier feedback clears fatal leakage in a hosted agent, and a three-seed ablation finds principle-only feedback clears decision-level defects, though these mitigation results are limited. LeakBench treats trustworthy clinical prediction as a property of an agent's modeling process, not merely its score; it is an audit testbed with known-failure controls, not yet an expert-validated benchmark.

items.title: Securing Agentic Commerce Through Behavior-Aware Fraud Detection and Cybersecurity for Trusted AI-Agent Payment Authorization
items.abstract_or_text: The growing use of autonomous artificial intelligence agents in digital commerce creates new security concerns involving agent impersonation, unauthorized payments, compromised agents, and misuse of delegated authority. This research introduces the Autonomous Commerce Agent Guard System (ACAGS), a cybersecurity framework combining supervised machine learning, behavioral analytics, agent-specific authorization controls, and explainable AI. The framework was evaluated using synthetic financial transaction data augmented with simulated agent characteristics and five adversarial scenarios. XGBoost was selected following comparisons with alternative classifiers. Across ten experimental runs, behavioral features improved mean F1-score from 52.12% to 67.49%, with agent-specific features increasing performance to 69.46%. The framework achieved detection rates of 99.77% for abnormal agent behavior, 99.73% for impersonation, and 100% for malicious delegation and authorization-scope violations. Compromised-agent detection reached 72.27%. ACAGS also supported APPROVE, REVIEW, and REJECT authorization outcomes, with SHAP explanations providing model interpretability. The results demonstrate the potential of combining behavioral intelligence and delegated authorization controls to strengthen simulated agentic-commerce payment security, while highlighting the need for validation using real-world transactions.

items.title: Guided Diffusion for Trustworthy Synthetic Text Generation
items.abstract_or_text: The rapid evolution of Large Language Models is fueled by massive datasets, yet this reliance poses severe privacy risks, as models can inadvertently memorize and even directly output sensitive training data. Synthetic text generation offers a promising solution to this challenge; however, existing methods struggle to reconcile rigorous privacy guarantees with high data utility. In this paper, we propose a new paradigm for private synthetic text generation: Guided Diffusion. Leveraging the unique steerability of Diffusion Language Models, we introduce novel sampling and re-masking procedures that actively guide the iterative denoising steps. These mechanisms steer the generative process to reconstruct fluent text that adheres to a target semantic distribution. We demonstrate that our framework is naturally compatible with Differential Privacy (DP): once the semantic embeddings of the private corpus are protected, the DP guarantee carries over to the generated text by post-processing. Empirically, we show that our approach generates high-quality synthetic text with precise semantic alignment. Furthermore, we validate its effectiveness in DP synthetic text generation: across two datasets and two diffusion backbones, it outperforms Private Evolution and DP-SGD-based fine-tuning in distributional fidelity and downstream utility, while generating significantly faster than Private Evolution. We further extend the framework to Data-Specific Indistinguishability (DSI), which adds a formal certificate against data poisoning and memorization at a small utility cost.

items.title: NIOCIS: Typed-Decision Next-Hop Routing with Node-Conditioned Option Spaces for Tool-Use Agents
items.abstract_or_text: Tool-use agents pay per decision: at each hop a language model re-reads the state and thinks for seconds, though its actions are finite and decisions recur. We present NIOCIS, a routing layer that folds execution logs into a loop-collapsed action graph (forward transitions plus recovery back-edges) answering one typed question: which declared option at a state, plus stop, does the fleet take next? A small model reads a calibrated distribution over them in one pass, emitting no text. On 1,615 production security-operations episodes we measure what the layer replaces, returns and is bounded by. Replaces: the typed encoder matches the logged next hop on 32.2% of the 3,875 held-out decisions (34.9% within the declared options) in 10 ms of encoder time (19.5 ms for the typed-choice form), against 2.2 s per LLM hop; two feature readouts reach 32.8% and 32.3%, an ordering the paired test does not resolve, so the typed layer is chosen for cost, not a separated lead. Tuning: jpt-4b reaches 9.9% zero-shot and 31.9% fine-tuned, a gap an exact paired test does not resolve (p=0.68), at 244 ms. Returns little: the realised hop falls outside the declared options for 7.9% of decisions and outside the model's top twenty for 9.3%; the most confident 15% holds 91.9% accuracy. Bounded: a cross-trace leave-one-out test puts the released state's ceiling at 25.6--44.9% as the state key grows more specific, i.e. repeated states disagree more often than they agree; the option-space ablation attributes the gain to per-node candidate restriction (+3.5 points over a flat catalog) rather than graph traversal (zero within its interval); a gated self-evolution loop lifts every arm above its anchor yet ends below full supervision; a confidence-gated cascade loses agreement when the escalation arm is the zero-shot stand-in; and agreement past a third of the fleet needs a state carrying the plan and the observation.

items.title: PFedQFT: Personalized Federated Quantum-Inspired Fine-Tuning for Medical Large Language Models
items.abstract_or_text: Medical data remain fragmented across institutional silos because of privacy, governance, and ownership constraints. Federated learning enables medical institutions to adapt large language models (LLMs) collaboratively without transferring raw records. However, independently parameterized low-rank adapters incur repeated parameter and communication costs across Transformer projections, while uniform aggregation may limit adaptation to heterogeneous institutional data. We propose PFedQFT, a quantum-inspired framework for personalized federated fine-tuning with a compact shared adapter. Specifically, PFedQFT constructs reusable orthonormal adaptation bases from compact skew-symmetric generators using a truncated matrix-exponential approximation followed by QR orthonormalization. Compatible projections reuse these bases, while a globally shared full core preserves the flexibility of each projection. Each client further maintains a lightweight private residual operator, whose directions are learned globally and whose coefficients remain local. Experiments on seven public medical tasks and multiple LLM backbones show substantial reductions in trainable parameters and per-round adapter upload volume, with competitive predictive performance on most tasks.

items.title: Metagenomic contextualization of proteins with state space models
items.abstract_or_text: Genomic foundation models have emerged as powerful tools for learning representations of biological sequences, but existing approaches predominantly rely on Transformer architectures, whose quadratic attention complexity limits their ability to capture long-range genomic context. This limitation is particularly relevant for metagenomics, where sequencing data have increased more than 500-fold since 2011, generating increasingly large and diverse datasets. For example, gLM2, a Transformer-based mixed-modality genomic language model, was trained with a context window of 4,096 tokens, limiting its ability to capture extended genomic context within metagenomic contigs. Developing scalable architectures capable of processing longer sequences while integrating protein and nucleotide information is therefore essential for advancing genomic foundation models. We introduce Nammu, a 167-million-parameter, bidirectional Mamba-based genomic foundation model that integrates protein and nucleotide sequences within a 20,000-token context window. Leveraging the linear scaling of state-space models, Nammu was trained using a curriculum learning strategy on the OpenMetaGenomic (OMG) corpus, first incorporating 64 million protein sequences followed by 32 million mixed-modality metagenomic contigs. Despite using approximately 37\% fewer training tokens than gLM2, Nammu outperformed this Transformer-based model in taxonomic classification across all evaluated taxonomic ranks on a marine metagenomic dataset from the Critical Assessment of Metagenome Interpretation (CAMI). On the exact-feature-unmatched CAMI II Strain Madness test set, Nammu achieved higher all-contig genus-classification accuracy than Kraken2 (0.9182 versus 0.8142). Nammu further outperformed gLM2 (150M) in KEGG Orthology prediction using deep-sea metagenome-assembled genomes. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of state-space architectures for scalable, multimodal genomic representation learning and highlight their ability to support accurate taxonomic and functional predictions from metagenomic sequences.

items.title: Generative discovery, symmetry-aware membership screening, and device-level evaluation of six-member-ring MoS2 polytypes
items.abstract_or_text: Six-membered-ring (SMR) inorganic materials were recently unified into a class, but the class-level perspective lacks two enabling tools: an operational test of “SMR-ness” and a path from newly generated crystals to device-level figures of merit. Here we couple conditional generative modelling (MatterGen; Mo–S, Ti–S, W–Se; 512 cells per system) to a novelty/stability funnel, a symmetry-aware membership checker that casts the SMR definition as three calibrated criteria (6/6 positives, 6/6 trap negatives), full DFT relaxation with composition-anchored hull analysis, and a contract-based device evaluation injecting literature-anchored OCV and diffusivity into an electrochemical cell model. The campaign maps the AA-stacked polytype manifold across five TMD chemistries, confirming 61 candidates (12 MoS2, 7 TiS2, 18 WSe2, 16 MoSe2, 8 NbS2; e.g. the MoS2 series P6̄m2, c = 7.1–40.8 Å, Ehull = 0.019–0.022 eV atom−1), 56 of them novel against every queried database. A dedicated spin cross-check (ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic and unpolarised initialisations) collapses to zero moments in every tested channel, and a three-probe stability screen (phonons, annealing dynamics, hull distance) shows the layered frameworks robust while the AA registry is metastable toward layer sliding, sharpening the synthesis list into kinetically stabilisable targets with two registry-robust entries. Two methodological findings transfer to any SMR screening effort: minimum-ring statistics collapse on TMD coordination (four-rings swallow six-rings), and membership is adjudicable only after relaxation. At the device end, material classes are discriminated by 0.639 V and polytypes by computed Li barriers (a 1.6× 10 8 diffusivity ratio separates fast from frozen at 0.5C); every number is traceable to a versioned experiment record.

items.title: FinHopper: A Progressive Multi-Hop Benchmark for Complex Financial Agents with Step-wise Evaluation
items.abstract_or_text: Financial agents are expected to answer factual investment queries through open search, but financial multi-hop retrieval differs from general multi-hop QA in a crucial way: each intermediate answer is an exact typed constraint, such as an entity, date, event, or numerical indicator, that determines the next query. This strict answer-conditioned dependency makes small intermediate errors cascade into plausible but wrong search trajectories. We introduce FinHopper, a benchmark for complex financial agents with controlled reasoning depth from 1 to 6 hops, covering stocks, funds, and macroeconomic facts, with gold intermediate answers for process-level evaluation. To construct FinHopper at scale, we design a state-transition-based synthesis framework that composes verified atomic financial QA patterns into dependency-preserving chains, followed by targeted in-synthesis verification, model-ensemble checking, and public-search validation by financial experts. Experiments with 20 LLM-agent configurations show that public search tools are necessary but insufficient: performance drops sharply as hop depth increases, the best model remains far below human experts, and process-aware scoring reveals partial reasoning progress hidden by final-answer-only evaluation. The benchmark is available at https://github.com/justajustin/FinHopper/.

items.title: An immune world model with multi-agent orchestration for peptide vaccines
items.abstract_or_text: Peptide-vaccine design requires a connection between vaccine-induced priming and recognition of the antigen naturally displayed by a tumor. We present an immune world model that preserves this connection through separate vaccine and tumor branches, endpoint-specific evidence and multi-agent orchestration. Native-recognition constraints held an altered peptide despite its higher presentation score, and targeted perturbations removed antigen-dependent benefit when required tumor-recognition conditions were absent. Public dendritic-cell data distinguished donor from antigen-source transfer: a context ranker achieved Recall@20 of 0.483 and 0.333 under the respective holdouts. Structure-informed receptor prediction added candidate-ranking evidence while preserving functional constraints and matched scenario trajectories. An assay observation model further concentrated a cross-presentation coefficient around its known value in a synthetic conditioning experiment. Together, these results establish a computational framework for linking molecular predictions, native-target requirements and conditional immune dynamics. The framework provides a reproducible basis for choosing peptide-vaccine candidates and the experiments needed to resolve their biological dependencies.

items.title: Toward Interpretable Graph-Based Machine Learning for Combustion Kinetic Model Generation
items.abstract_or_text: This work presents an atom-conserving and interpretable graph neural network (GNN) for combustion kinetic model generation, where atoms are represented as nodes, covalent bonds are represented as edges, and reactions are represented as bond-rearrangement operations. Its artificial-intelligence (AI) contribution is a reaction generator that extends a standard Graph Isomorphism Network with Edges (GINE) architecture through reaction-context embeddings, reaction branching & third-body reaction inputs, Arrhenius-rate-parameter prediction, pairwise decoding, and stochastic inference over evolving reactant pools. Trained on the Li–Dryer hydrogen combustion kinetic model (8 species and 21 reactions), the GNN reproduces trained chemistry and generates element-balanced new reactions and intermediate species outside the training dataset, many of which have experimental analogues. When trained on a subset of the Li–Dryer dataset, the model recovered most held-out reactions and revealed relationships between samples (reactions) in the model’s latent space. The results suggest that the model learns transferable local reaction structures and generates valid species and reactions. As with any reaction generators, the generated reaction models require thermochemical and kinetic verification; the intended engineering application is low-cost reaction-pathway exploration for new fuels and prioritization of experiments and first-principles calculations to develop new combustion kinetic models.

items.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
items.abstract_or_text: Large Language Model (LLM) agents can handle increasingly complex tasks, navigating long trajectories of observations and actions. As these trajectories grow, key-value (KV) cache I/O and storage become the dominant cost. Trajectories can also exceed the LLM's maximum context length, requiring control over active cache growth. Prior work uses context engineering to reduce cache size by trimming or summarizing history. However, modifying the trajectory prefix invalidates subsequent cached states and triggers costly re-prefilling of retained context. Task accuracy can also suffer when too little context is retained to limit re-prefill costs. We propose cache engineering as a new scheme. It allows agents to directly control their active KV cache without modifying the trajectory or re-prefilling retained context. Specifically, agents can proactively use drop to exclude selected cache from future attention and repos to adjust retained keys' position encodings. We formalize these cache operations and identify history dependence as a serving challenge: identical token sequences can yield different cache states under different cache operation sequences, making prefix matching insufficient for correct cache reuse. Thus, we co-design the AKV serving engine. It provides a stateless interface compatible with existing serving APIs, while internally managing stateful cache reuse, eviction, and restoration. Experiments show that a tool-response rolling-drop cache policy improves average benchmark scores by 1.7 points and reduces average cost by 27.7%, compared with conventional threshold-triggered summarization. With AKV, it achieves up to 1.2x the output throughput and a 1.5x speedup in P95 request latency. Recursive self-improvement of cache policies further reduces cost by 7.1% over expert design. Our code is at https://github.com/thu-nics/AKV.

items.title: Building Telecom Language Models with RSOD: Domain Data, Specialist Post-Training, Memory-Conscious Distillation, and Networking Evaluation
items.abstract_or_text: Telecom language models must combine broad networking knowledge with specialist behavior across routing, broadband services, access technologies, and operational diagnostics while remaining practical to deploy as a single model. We present an end-to-end framework that builds source-grounded synthetic training data from structured networking taxonomies and expert graphs, materializes 212,559 routed training records across fourteen networking routes, trains six frozen specialist LoRA teachers over one shared continued-pretrained backbone, and consolidates their behavior into one deployable student adapter using Routed Specialist On-Policy Distillation (RSOD). In RSOD, the committed student generates each trajectory, the route-assigned specialist teacher-forces the exact native token sequence, compact teacher hidden states are reconstructed through the shared frozen output head, and only the student LoRA is updated. A controlled reconstruction validation shows mean absolute logit error of 7.26 x 10^-6 with 100% top-1 agreement between native and reconstructed teacher logits. On four RTX 6000 Ada GPUs, the completed 2,000-step run produced 16,000 trajectories with zero observed student-version or token- ID mismatches. Under the primary route-conditioned evaluation over 2,850 held-out questions, the raw Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model scores 12.8661/25 micro (13.0172/25 macro), the combined routed six-teacher system scores 21.7641/25 micro, and the consolidated RSOD student, released as Llama-CalixCLM v1, reaches 21.7112/25 micro (21.8006/25 macro) on the same five dimension LLM-judge rubric. Under a separate neutral deployment-like prompt, the same student reaches 20.0028/25 micro (20.0778/25 macro). The consolidated student remains within 0.0529 micro-score points of the combined routed-teacher system while retaining a numerically validated and auditable train-serve execution path.

items.title: Pharmacologic inhibition of OLIG2 by CT-179 disrupts mitotic progression and enhances standard-of-care chemoradiotherapy in glioblastoma
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains uniformly fatal. The basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor OLIG2 is universally expressed in diffuse glioma, sustains the tumor-propagating stem-like fraction, and opposes p53-mediated genotoxic responses, but has historically been considered undruggable. We characterized CT-179, a brain-penetrant small-molecule OLIG2 inhibitor, as a candidate therapeutic for GBM. Methods: Target engagement was assessed by cellular thermal shift assay, differential scanning fluorimetry, crosslinking, and electrophoretic mobility shift assay. Anti-tumor activity was evaluated across eleven patient-derived GBM cell lines, in zebrafish oligodendrocyte precursor cell (OPC)-derived tumors, and orthotopic and subcutaneous GBM models, including combinations with radiotherapy plus temozolomide and with selective Bcl-2 family inhibitors. Results: CT-179 engaged OLIG2 and altered the conformation of dimerized OLIG2 on chromatin without preventing dimerization or fully displacing OLIG2 from DNA. CT-179 reduced OLIG2-positive OPCs and OPC-derived tumors in zebrafish and inhibited proliferation across all eleven GBM lines (IC50 < 360 nM), depleting the stem-like fraction and inducing apoptosis through mitotic catastrophe, mitotic slippage, or a hybrid response. RNA-seq across three patient-derived glioma stem cell lines identified {beta}-tubulin gene isoforms as the most strongly CT-179-down-regulated transcripts at the early time point and showed correlated {beta}-tubulin and OLIG2 expression in TCGA glioblastoma specimens. Combination with the Mcl-1 inhibitor S63845 or the Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Bcl-w inhibitor ABT-737 produced greater-than-additive cytotoxicity. Oral CT-179 crossed the blood-brain barrier and extended median survival as a single agent across two independent adult orthotopic patient-derived backgrounds (GBM8 and G06); intraperitoneal CT-179 was associated with reduced intratumoral OLIG2 and Ki-67 staining in GBM8 orthotopic xenografts. Combination of CT-179 with radiotherapy and temozolomide eliminated all GBM8 and 7 of 8 GBM4 subcutaneous xenografts without weight loss and significantly extended survival when combined with radiotherapy in MGMT-unmethylated GBM6 orthotopic xenografts (CT-179 administered intraperitoneally). Conclusions: CT-179 is a brain-penetrant inhibitor of an established GBM driver with single-agent and combination activity across several orthotopic models, supporting clinical development for GBM and translational evaluation in other OLIG2-dependent CNS malignancies.

items.title: Quantum Coherence in Guest-Controlled Endohedral Fullerenes: Hierarchical Equations of Motion and a Neural-Network Model.
items.abstract_or_text: Light-harvesting efficiency hinges on how long an excitation stays coherent, yet in natural antennae the environment that destroys that coherence, the protein scaffold, cannot be redesigned at will. Here we invert the architecture and place the bath inside the chromophore: a C60 cage acts as the absorber while an encapsulated guest (CH4, N2, O2 or H2O) supplies a tunable internal environment. Combining B3LYP/6-31G* excitation energies, transition-electrostatic-potential (TrESP) couplings and hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM), we find that the choice of guest alone dictates the character of the dynamics. The guest acts through three parameters: the excitonic coupling to the neighbouring cage, the shift of the cage excitation energy and the reorganisation energy (λ). The damping of quantum beats grows in proportion to λ, coherent exchange gives way to incoherent hopping once λkBT/ℏγ becomes comparable to the coupling, and the guest-induced shifts of the excitation energy set the direction of net energy flow. Pairs containing the polar H2O guest, with λ above 40 cm−1, lie in the incoherent regime, whereas O2@C60, 5750 cm−1 below the other cages, is isolated from them. Two-dimensional electronic spectra of the all-system endohedral fullerenes show beats at the exciton gaps and spectral diffusion on the 100 fs time scale of the bath. We further demonstrate that this mapping can be inverted. A feed-forward neural network trained on a corpus of 3000 HEOM trajectories recovers a dimer’s site-energy gap, excitonic coupling and λ from a single 2 ps trace, with mean absolute errors of 3.45, 1.87 and 1.13 cm−1 on 600 unseen realisations. The coherence must accompany the population, because the sign of the coupling is reversed by a gauge transformation that leaves the populations unchanged; supplied with ρ12(t), the network recovers it in every held-out case. Internalising the bath thus renders coherence both tunable by design and readable from the dynamics.

items.title: MoSAIK: Motion Search with Artificial Intelligence in K-space
items.abstract_or_text: Object: Motion artefacts remain a major limitation of routine two-dimensional T2-weighted turbo spin-echo (TSE) brain MRI, reducing diagnostic confidence and often necessitating repeated acquisitions. MoSAIK (Motion Search with AI in K-space) retrospectively estimates in-plane rigid-body motion directly from standard multi-coil TSE k-space. Without a motion-free reference, external navigators, or additional acquisitions, MoSAIK infers motion from k-space self-consistency violations and incorporates predicted parameters into model-based, motion-aware reconstruction rather than synthesizing corrected images. Materials and Methods: Selected complex coil data were represented as log-magnitude and phase channels. A decoupled convolutional embedding and Transformer encoder estimated phase-encoding-line-indexed rotation and two-dimensional translations. Training used motion-free clinical acquisitions with simulated motion; four held-out subjects were evaluated. Component-wise errors assessed estimation; SSIM and PSNR in silico and entropy focus criterion (EFC) in vivo assessed reconstruction. Results: Motion estimation errors were low for both rotation (MSE < 0.2 deg^2) and translation (MSE < 0.2 pixels^2), with Pearson correlations of approximately 0.96 and 0.94, respectively. In every in-vivo acquisition, more than 75% of slices showed information gain relative to uncorrected reconstructions. MoSAIK reduced visible artefacts while preserving anatomical detail. Discussion: Transformer-based k-space motion-trajectory estimation enables fast retrospective correction of standard clinical TSE brain MRI.

items.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
items.abstract_or_text: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks. We therefore propose Agent World Model in the Wild (WildAWM), a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks for training general computer-use agents (CUAs). Whereas existing approaches typically specialize in a single agent interaction interface, we construct executable environments that jointly support graphical user interfaces, model context protocol services, and command-line interfaces, allowing agents to flexibly combine visual interaction, tool use, and code execution. WildAWM is entirely powered by open-source models, demonstrating that high-quality computer-use environments can be generated without proprietary frontier models. Beyond environments, we address three recurring challenges in task synthesis: ensuring solvability, maintaining sufficient difficulty, and producing reliable verifiers, by introducing execution-based quality gates that combine heterogeneous agent rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, and counterfactual probes of judgment robustness. The resulting pipeline synthesizes 341 long-horizon environment-task pairs that can require over 100 agent steps to solve and remain challenging even for frontier models, with GPT-6-Astra solving only 60% of them. We train two Qwen models of different sizes exclusively in these synthetic worlds. Both models achieve substantial gains across 8 out-of-distribution benchmarks spanning web, claw, and computer-use agents, demonstrating that learning in WildAWM's synthesized worlds generalizes broadly to unseen computer-use tasks. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/MSR-Orchard/WildAWM.

items.title: Contextual Biomedical Language Models for Imbalance-Aware Drug-Food Interaction Classification
items.abstract_or_text: Drug-food interactions (DFIs) are essential to patient safety because they can alter drug effectiveness or cause side effects. Automated classification of DFIs is difficult because of unstructured textual data, semantic ambiguity, and class imbalance, especially when separating neutral interactions. This paper presents an imbalance-aware deep learning approach for classifying drug-food interactions into three classes: safe, neutral, and unsafe. A structured dataset is created from textual drug interaction descriptions by extracting drug-food pairs and labeling them using rule-based heuristics. To address class imbalance, we apply class weighting and focal loss while fine-tuning the context-aware BioBERT language model. Our experiments show that the approach reaches an accuracy of 85% and a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.77, with a notable improvement on the minority neutral class (F1-score of 0.56). The main novelty of this work is the combination of contextual biomedical language modeling with imbalance-aware deep learning, enabling more effective classification of DFI datasets.

items.title: A Novel Reactive Incipient Wetness Impregnation Assisted by H 2 O 2 for Vanadium Catalysts: the Case of V/Silicalite-1 zeolites in Oxidative Propane Dehydrogenation
items.abstract_or_text: Metal deposition in zeolites is often interpreted using concepts developed for relatively open support surfaces, overlooking the consequences of precursor transport and deposition within confined microporous environments. Here, we introduce an H 2 O 2 -mediated reactive impregnation strategy for supported vanadium catalysts reactive vanadium impregnation mediated by H 2 O 2 and that avoids organics complexing agents (carbon-free) exploiting vanadium-peroxo chemistry to dissolve in situ the precursor into smaller complexed soluble species and modify its interaction with Silicalite-1. The resulting catalyst displayed still detectable vanadium aggregates compared with conventional impregnation. The materials tested under oxidative propane dehydrogenation exhibited comparable catalytic activity (slightly higher) but improved stability during repeated reaction-regeneration cycling. The in situ coke accumulation within a cycle was tracked in the intermediary regeneration steps by using online MS, and showed similar amounts for both preparation routes, suggesting that carbon deposition is governed predominantly by the structural and pore-capacity characteristics of Silicalite-1. Structural characterization revealed distinct vanadium-support interactions in the H 2 O 2 -assisted materials, while microscopy and H2-TPR indicated different evolution of the support and vanadium phase during cycling. Under representative OPDH conditions, the H 2 O 2 -assisted catalyst reached 41% propane conversion and 90% propylene selectivity, with a 30% lower deactivation rate over ten cycles. These results identify precursor chemistry and metal-support interaction, rather than dispersion alone, as key design parameters for supported vanadium catalysts.

items.title: An open-source electrosynthesis platform for reaction screening enables a nickel-catalyzed electroreductive aryl cyanation
items.abstract_or_text: The application of electrochemistry to synthetic organic chemistry has resulted in the development of more efficient and sustainable synthesis methodologies. However, the costs and technical burdens of electrochemical instrumentation impose barriers towards the wider adoption of electrochemistry. Herein, we report a modular, open-source platform for electrosynthesis screening built around a low-cost miniaturized potentiostat. The platform supports electrosynthesis and electroanalytic methods, and its open design readily allows for customization. We demonstrate this utility of the platform by the development of a zinc-free, nickel-catalyzed reductive cyanation of aryl bromides with an electrophilic cyanating agent (2-methyl-2-phenylmalononitrile, MPMN). Replacing stoichiometric zinc reductant with a sacrificial tertiary amine allows the cyanation of aryl bromides incompatible with the original zinc-based conditions. In addition, acetonitrile can be used in place of typical hazardous amide solvents. This work provides a blueprint for non-expert practitioners to integrate electrochemistry as an accessible and affordable technique in their research programs.

items.title: Manifold-Informed Neural Networks for Low-Label ECG Electrolyte Inference
items.abstract_or_text: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) supervise on the residual of a known differential operator. Many high-stakes inference problems admit no such operator: clinical signals, behavioral measurements, materials properties. We introduce the Manifold-Informed Neural Network (MINN), a PINN-parallel paradigm that replaces the physics operator residual with a manifold operator residual: a discrete Poisson equation L_G H = s_φ(x, m) on a k-nearest-neighbor graph in the learned latent space, with a learned, task-aware source. The construction is a structural parallel to PINNs (squared operator residual plus label data, in place of operator residual plus boundary data); the s{=}0 limit recovers the homogeneous Laplace equation L_GH=0 (classical manifold regularization solves the same equation but minimizes the Dirichlet energy tr(H^\topL_GH), a different penalty form). The source s_φ takes input features and auxiliary metadata directly, breaking the homogeneous smoothness prior that limits classical Laplacian penalties; gated Feature-wise Linear Modulation separately fuses metadata into the prediction branch. We evaluate MINN on three-class classification of potassium, calcium, and magnesium from 12-lead ECGs in MIMIC-IV-ECG, against twelve baselines spanning supervised and tabular methods, ECG foundation models, and manifold/graph approaches. MINN attains the highest K^+ Macro-F1 of 0.61 (best baseline 0.55), with consistent gains on Ca^{2+} and Mg^{2+} and a 31% relative improvement at 1% labeled data. Six targeted ablations show that the inhomogeneous Poisson formulation, not graph smoothing alone, drives the gain.

items.title: BAIT: Can LLMs Find What Biases a Reader? A Benchmark for Cognitive Bias Triggers in News
items.abstract_or_text: Persuasive writing exploits cognitive biases, recruiting a reader's mental shortcuts to shape belief, often without the reader noticing. We call the linguistic features exploiting such mental shortcuts cognitive bias triggers. As large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people encounter news, summarizing it, ranking it, and answering questions over it, a natural question is whether they can recognize the features of a text that bias a human reader. We introduce BAIT (Bias Annotation In Text), a resource for detecting cognitive bias triggers in news. BAIT pairs a schema of nine triggers, each specified in an annotator codebook, with 50 English news articles annotated by trained annotators at the article and span levels and adjudicated into a gold standard. On this data we define two tasks, detecting which triggers a text contains and locating the spans that carry them. We then benchmark six frontier LLMs zero-shot and with three or ten in-context examples. The models approach human agreement on which triggers an article contains, but rarely recover its full set of triggers, and they reach less than half of human agreement in locating the passages that carry them. Moreover, they over-predict triggers that come with easy surface cues, and most of the passages they mark for these triggers are not triggers, yet carry the trigger's surface cue far more often than random text. These findings suggest that the evaluated LLMs respond to surface cues rather than to the mechanisms that make a passage manipulative. We release the schema, the codebook, standoff annotations, and the evaluation pipeline.

items.title: A Unified Attack Framework against Statistical Generative Watermarks for Large Language Models
items.abstract_or_text: Watermarking has emerged as a key tool for identifying text generated by large language models (LLMs), with current schemes embedding statistical signals into the generation process to enable later detection. In this work, we identify a shared weakness across a broad class of popular LLM watermarking methods, including KGW (and its variants), GumbelSoft, DipMark, ITS, and SynthID. We show that these schemes exhibit a fundamental link between their detection scores and the token probability shifts they introduce during generation. This link, which we call score-ratio alignment, allows an attacker with only black-box query access to the model--and no knowledge of secret keys or model weights--to produce text that evades detection while remaining fluent and natural. We prove that the resulting attack is optimal across all covered watermark families, and show that the weakness is intrinsic: any watermark designed to maximize statistical detection power necessarily induces the very structure that attackers can exploit. We evaluate our attack on seven popular generative LLM watermarking schemes, three LLMs, and tasks, which reduce detection rates to at most 0.05 across all settings while preserving text quality. Our findings show that current watermarking methods can be reliably defeated under realistic attack conditions, highlighting the need for fundamentally different watermarking designs that decouple detection scores from token probability shifts.

items.title: RaspAssistant as an Agentic Framework for Automating Adsorption Simulation Research in Porous Materials
items.abstract_or_text: Porous-material adsorption studies require coordinated structure preparation, force-field selection, simulation, validation, and interpretation, making end-to-end automation difficult. We test whether RaspAssistant, a hierarchical multi-agent framework, can carry an adsorption study from force-field preparation through validation and downstream separation analysis. Across twelve multi-agent workflow-reproduction runs spanning four adsorption and separation benchmarks, overall scores ranged from 8.50 to 10.00 on a rubric evaluating workflow correctness, simulation validity, and analysis consistency. In a separate eight-case force-field extraction benchmark, the mean weighted score was 0.967, combining parameter agreement and RASPA readiness. In open-ended studies, the system diagnosed and refined an acetylene force field and, after validating a CO_2 force field against MFI experiments, screened 197 pure-silica zeolites that passed automated input checks. These results demonstrate autonomous workflow execution after task specification and input provision: RaspAssistant coordinates, validates, adapts, and documents extended adsorption-simulation workflows while exposing model sensitivity and methodological limitations for expert review.

items.title: Learning the Geometry of Materials Space with Trained Neural Tangent Kernels
items.abstract_or_text: Neural networks trained to predict materials properties learn representations whose physical content can be difficult to extract. We use the neural tangent kernel (NTK), evaluated at trained parameters, to recover the geometry learned by a network that predicts superconducting transition temperatures from elemental composition alone. Kernel ridge regression with the trained NTK closely reproduces the network's predictive performance and substantially outperforms regression with the initial kernel. Spectral analysis and multidimensional scaling reveal a geometry dominated by a small number of directions. Clustering and local neighborhood analysis organize compounds into recognizable superconducting families and connect materials with related chemical and correlated-electron properties despite substantial differences in T_c. These results establish trained tangent kernels as practical probes of learned materials representations, connecting property prediction with the exploration of materials space.

items.title: MultiCard: Multiple Attribute Cardinality Estimation via Deep Learning
items.abstract_or_text: Cardinality estimation is essential for query optimization, but most existing learned estimators focus on a single predicate type, such as string LIKE clauses or numerical range filters. In practice, analytical workloads often combine both types, while the accuracy of string estimators tends to decrease with longer patterns. We introduce MultiCard, a comprehensive learned cardinality estimator that unifies LIKE predicates and numerical filters within a single end-to-end architecture. By combining a Transformer for long-range sparse patterns with an LSTM for short, frequent patterns, MultiCard achieves robust pattern modeling. In parallel, a numerical encoder integrates catalog histograms and structural predicate features, enabling the model to dynamically assess histogram estimation accuracy across different operators and data skew conditions. A final Transformer layer captures interactions among heterogeneous predicates before a multilayer perceptron predicts query cardinalities. We also introduce UPCI, a workload generator that produces length-balanced LIKE patterns, multi-column numerical predicates, and exact cardinality labels for training and evaluation. Experiments on five real-world datasets show that, for string-only workloads, MultiCard achieves the best or near-best Q-error across all datasets compared with state-of-the-art methods. For mixed multi-attribute queries, MultiCard reduces PostgreSQL's mean Q-error by up to 16 times while maintaining an inference latency below 5 ms.

items.title: Decision4Rec: A Jev-Inspired Framework of Decision Models on Knowledge and Active Graphs for Multi-Agent Recommender Systems
items.abstract_or_text: Decision models, such as the commercial Jev, are language models that return one probability for each option of a question instead of generating text. We present Decision4Rec, an open and modular framework that makes decision models useful for recommendation. A knowledge graph writes the logs of each recommendation scenario as short statements on a defined scale, such as "sold: top 10%". A pool of agents, proposes candidates, and a residual ranker keeps the best 30. A decision model, trained once on real choices of three scenarios, reads them through one interface of typed questions, and a fusion step combines its answers with the score of the ranker. Any model with this interface can be used, and we run the commercial Jev, the released open Kev and Kev models trained by us on recommendation requests. The framework with a trained 4B decision model is 25 to 36% above the best trained baseline in NDCG@10 in three sparse Amazon catalogues, one of them never used to train the decision model, and almost tie with baselines on the dense Steam dataset. Most of the gain comes from the pool, and with a trained recommender it comes from what the agents know about its candidates rather than from new candidates. The 27B decision model adds to the pool 5 to 6% above the 0.8B model in three of four domains. A trained 0.8B open model beats the released Jev in eleven of fifteen settings and is never worse. On MovieLens-1M, a dense domain never seen in training, the gain is 5 to 7%. Code, configurations and trained models are available at https://github.com/marcopoli/decision4rec and https://huggingface.co/m-polignano.

items.title: Determinants of cysteine coverage by chemoproteomics
items.abstract_or_text: Covalent chemoproteomics has become a powerful route to expanding the druggable proteome, enabling proteome-wide screening of compounds that covalently modify nucleophilic residues, most commonly cysteine. Yet typical experiments detect only 5-18% of the ~250,000 cysteines encoded by the human proteome, and the determinants of this limited coverage remain poorlydefined. Here we combine cysteine featurisation, explainable machine learning (ML) and robust statistical filtering to establish what governs cysteine detectability in iodoacetamide- desthiobiotin (IA-DTB) chemoproteomics. Using a scalable feature-generation pipeline, we computed physicochemical and structural properties for cysteines and the corresponding tryptic peptides and trained models that predict detectability with high accuracy. Shapley analysis identifies protein abundance and intrinsic peptide properties governing LC-MS behaviour as the dominant determinants, whereas cysteine structural descriptors contribute comparatively little, indicating that detection is constrained downstream of probe reactivity. We further introduce a distance-based statistical filter that improves reproducibility across replicates, and show that cell line selection, subcellular fractionation and alternative electrophiles together expand coverage by >30%. More broadly, this work moves optimisation of chemoproteomics workflows from empirical trial-and-error towards rational, data-driven design.

items.title: Curriculum Learning for Generative Flexible Docking
items.abstract_or_text: Flexible docking is a highly practical task, aiming to predict the joint configuration of a protein-ligand complex from a protein apo structure and a ligand SMILES string. Diffusion and flow-based generative models have made this task tractable by modeling the posterior distribution over the ligand pose and the protein conformation conditioned on the apo input. The central challenge, however, remains the long-tailed apo-to-holo structure shift, where a small fraction of protein undergo large conformational changes. In this work, motivated by the practical observation that downweighting large shift examples improves generalization, and by the mixed nature of the long tail consisting of genuinely difficult examples and noisy ones, we propose to use curriculum learning for this task, gradually incorporating large conformational change examples during training. With a linear pacing function, we show that an existing method can be strongly enhanced. On the PDBBind ESMFold apo benchmark, with relaxation and confidence-based pose selection, the resulting model GCLDock achieves a 46.52% top-1 success rate (ligand RMSD less than 2A) and 40.26% when additionally requiring PoseBusters validity, outperforming existing baselines.

items.title: CUA-Recovery: Benchmarking Error Recovery in Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
items.abstract_or_text: As computer-use agents (CUAs) move to long-horizon workflows spanning multiple applications, undetected errors can silently corrupt persistent state and cause cascading failures in subsequent actions. Reliable error detection and recovery have become critical bottlenecks for building robust CUAs. However, existing benchmarks focus primarily on end-to-end task performance, providing limited insight into whether agents can detect and recover from errors during execution. The few benchmarks that evaluate recovery rely largely on manually injected errors, which may not reflect the types or horizons of failures induced by real agent policies. We introduce CUA-Recovery, a benchmark comprising test and training suites across multiple desktop applications. We construct it using ReRail, a framework for synthesizing long-horizon tasks and trajectories in a persistent desktop environment. ReRail composes MyPCBench tasks into new long-horizon workflows with executable ground truth, collects verifier-confirmed failures from multiple policies, and turns them into verified recovery trajectories. CUA-Recovery comprises a human-verified test suite of 2,250 erroneous states over 100 tasks and a training suite of 8.6K trajectories over 377 tasks. Evaluation on the test suite shows that agents struggle both to recognize inherited errors and to complete the task. Across six agents and six takeover depths, Error Awareness Rate (EAR) reaches at most 44.0% and Pass@3 at most 25.5%. After fine-tuning Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on the training suite, its average EAR rises from 19.9% to 35.2% on held-out recovery states, and its Rubric Score goes from 5.0% to 16.1%. It also gains 15.3 points on MyPCBench and 10.8 points on Odysseys for Pass@3, showing that the training trajectories help both with recovery and with completing tasks from a clean start. Our code is available at https://github.com/xu-hu-2002/CUA-Recovery.

items.title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
items.abstract_or_text: Accurate multi-horizon photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for grid stability, energy scheduling, and the efficient operation of PVbatterygrid systems. However, existing models often fail to jointly capture short-term variability and long-term temporal patterns, while lacking unified multi-horizon capability and interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and N-BEATS within an attention-based fusion architecture. The proposed model leverages TFT to learn short-term temporal dependencies and dynamic feature importance, while N-BEATS captures long-term trend and seasonal components through interpretable basis decomposition. An adaptive attention mechanism dynamically fuses both branches, enabling balanced multi-scale learning. The framework simultaneously generates forecasts for 30-minute, 2-hour, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour horizons within a single unified pipeline. The model is evaluated using multi-year real-world datasets from the Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC). Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over statistical, machine learning, and deep learning baselines. The proposed model achieves RMSE values of 42.35, 46.27, 52.29, and 48.11 across the 20162017, 2023, 2024, and 20252026 datasets, respectively, corresponding to a 3540% reduction compared to the best baseline (TFT). Additionally, MAPE remains below 5% across all datasets, indicating high predictive accuracy and stability. The model also provides interpretability through attention visualization and trendseasonality decomposition, and is deployed on a cloud-based platform for real-time forecasting. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework is robust, interpretable, and suitable for practical renewable energy applications.

items.title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
items.abstract_or_text: Machine learning is widely regarded as a promising application in which quantum computing could offer a computational advantage. However, general quantum machine learning models with provable guarantees on performance, trainability, and efficient inference remain limited. In this work, we introduce quantum Hamiltonian embeddings, a supervised learning framework in which a classical training dataset is encoded into a single effective, parameterized Hamiltonian. Training optimizes the parameters of this data-dependent Hamiltonian, whose approximate ground state defines the classification rule. Once the ground state has been approximated using a quantum algorithm, inference can be performed either classically using a classical representation of the learned state, or with a quantum representation of the state. We establish efficient methods for gradient estimation and prove favorable generalization guarantees. Furthermore, under standard cryptographic assumptions, we show that Hamiltonian embeddings can realize hypothesis functions beyond the reach of efficient classical algorithms. We then demonstrate the framework at scale on IBM Heron processors using a standard benchmark dataset. Together, these results establish Hamiltonian embeddings as a new framework for quantum machine learning, combining theoretical guarantees with a path for experimental investigations at scale on quantum hardware.

items.title: Honeyed Words, Hidden Daggers: Benchmarking and Training LLMs to See Through Mock Politeness
items.abstract_or_text: The Chinese idiom "kou mi fu jian" ("honeyed words, hidden daggers") names speech that is polite in form but hostile in function. We present ZhenhuanBench, a 1,592-item benchmark built from expert commentary on Empresses in the Palace, covering speaker intent, emotion-language mismatch, and per-listener uptake. Text-only evaluation covers 34 LLMs. GPT-6 Astra leads the leaderboard at 73.48% overall, while its listener-reaction score is 58.37%. The annotations also supply supervised traces and string-verifiable training rewards. With 338 gold traces, an 8B model outperforms teacher distillation on identical items. Subsequent RL saturates, and chance correction reduces the estimated recoverable performance gap by a factor of 7.5. Our CPR-GRPO loop (Compress-Probe-Replenish) uses this estimate to weight gold supervision, reaching 67.0 on public multiple-choice tasks and 74.5 under the training-matched hidden protocol. Without target-task training, CPR outperforms Base, SFT, and GRPO across six Chinese and English pragmatic and sarcasm evaluations. On three external datasets, training with CPR yields higher mean Macro-F1 than SFT and GRPO.

items.title: ORBIT: Autoregressive Time Series Generation via Next Frequency-Band Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Deep generative models provide an effective modern solution to alleviating the problem of data scarcity by synthesizing realistic time series. However, despite the considerable progress achieved by existing deep time series generators, two key challenges remain: (1) learning hierarchical representations for heterogeneous temporal patterns; and (2) coordinating the generation process of heterogeneous temporal dynamics. To address these key bottlenecks, in this work, we propose ORBIT, a unified deep generative framework for time series. Specifically, we develop two key components: the Frequency-Hierarchical VQ-VAE (FH-VQ-VAE) and the Frequency-Band Autoregressive Transformer (FBAR). The former learns hierarchical representations by decomposing latent temporal representations into different frequency bands and applying residual quantization with increasing token budgets. The latter establishes a novel low-to-high frequency autoregressive direction, yielding a time series generation process that first constructs global temporal structures and then incrementally incorporates fine-grained temporal details. These compact designs not only disentangle heterogeneous temporal patterns for more effective representation learning but also mitigate potential interference among different temporal dynamics during generation. Extensive experiments on multiple challenging real-world benchmarks demonstrate that ORBIT achieves state-of-the-art overall performance while exhibiting superior inference efficiency compared with advanced baselines.

items.title: EmbodiedWorld-200K: Toward Embodied World Agents via Embodied-Planning Dataset and Interactive World Models
items.abstract_or_text: Building embodied agents that can perceive, reason, and act across diverse 3D worlds is a central research direction toward artificial general intelligence. Yet most existing work remains confined to specific tasks in a single scene and transfers poorly to new environments, leaving general embodied agents for open-world settings under-explored. We refer to such agents as Embodied World Agents (EWAs), whose defining property is the ability to understand diverse visual environments and execute general actions in open-world conditions. To advance EWA research, we study open-world embodied navigation-planning and release EmbodiedWorld-200K, a large-scale dataset of over 200K samples spanning diverse scenes. Each example is equipped with multi-level annotations, ranging from low-level camera-motion trajectories to high-level semantic instructions. The dataset also provides unified evaluation splits and task-specific metrics, supporting offline pretraining and fair evaluation of EWAs. Beyond offline supervision, a defining characteristic of an EWA is its interaction with the environment; training solely on offline data is therefore insufficient, especially for generalizing to scenes not covered in the training distribution. Building dedicated real interactive environments, however, is often prohibitively expensive. To address this, we propose a novel training scheme that employs a video world model as a low-cost environment proxy and performs interactive reinforcement-learning (RL) post-training of the EWA within it.
